summary: @ornikar/prettier-config preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a Prettier configuration but its package.json declares a preinstall hook running an obfuscated setup.mjs. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/... into a temp directory, chmod +x's the extracted binary, and invokes it against a bundled math_init.js file. math_init.js is a 727 KB obfuscator.io-style payload (rotated string array via a WV8StW shift routine and an n7gIxM dictionary, `_0x...` identifiers) whose contents cannot be inspected without deobfuscation. setup.mjs itself is obfuscated with hex-numbered identifiers and per-function string maps. A Prettier configuration package has no legitimate reason to install a second language runtime, ship a 727 KB obfuscated JS payload, or obfuscate its install script. The preinstall lifecycle causes fetch-and-execute of attacker-controlled code on every `npm install` of this package, using Bun as an alternate runtime to evade Node-based scanners and analysis.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
